recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-35805 unless the PA work group later chooses to revise the guidance substantively.
issue_request: FHIR-35805 was an Applied/Persuasive PA change request asking for clearer guidance on when an Organization should represent a service as one HealthcareService with multiple Location references versus multiple HealthcareService resources, and how to choose between HealthcareService and Location contact/availability/endpoint details.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied before this reconciliation: commit c7f71ebf75ce9066bfd5389f6e73affa16f9fee4 added the 'Single or Multiple Locations' section to source/healthcareservice/healthcareservice-notes.xml, and merge commit 0cf428e3e2873b4d65e42acfdd11e7e6f083edd9 included the Jira-tagged change. Git history shows no later commits changing the HealthcareService notes file.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists both Location and HealthcareService as active resources, so the inspected notes file is in current build scope. The current notes section covers the approved considerations: availability hours, contact details, endpoint details, location characteristics, coverage areas, downstream split/merge management, one HealthcareService when details are shared, and omitting HealthcareService contact/availability/endpoint details when the Location details are the same. PA Confluence minutes from January 2022 record the discussion and intended notes guidance, and May 2023 minutes record the Persuasive 3-0-0 tracker handling. Jira neighborhood search found only FHIR-35805 for the same HealthcareService/Location availability/contact/multiple-location question, and direct Zulip issue-key search found no messages.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already implements the FHIR-35805 resolution closely enough to preserve implementer understanding, and further edits would be editorial rather than necessary reconciliation work.
